ai.definition: Photovoltaic panels that convert sunlight directly into electricity using crystalline silicon cells.
ai.howItWorks: Purified silicon is cast into ingots, sliced into wafers, doped to form a p–n junction, then assembled into glass-covered modules with anti-reflective coatings.
ai.problemSolved: Generation of clean, renewable electricity from sunlight.
ai.manufacturing: Silicon purification, casting, wafering, doping, module assembly.
ai.buildProcess: Purification, casting, slicing, doping, cell production, module assembly, anti-reflective coating application.
ai.costDrivers: Silicon raw material cost, manufacturing equipment and labor, energy consumption during production, quality control measures.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: continuing growth with advancements in efficiency and cost reduction.
ai.regulation: Varies by region; often includes incentives for renewable energy adoption.
ai.risks: Supply chain disruptions, technological obsolescence, environmental impact of manufacturing processes.
ai.profitability: High due to decreasing costs and increasing demand, but margins can be thin.
ai.futureDevelopment: Focus on efficiency improvements, recycling silicon materials, reducing production costs, and integrating with energy storage solutions.

glossary.def: A semiconductor interface where the p-type (positive) and n-type (negative) regions meet to facilitate the flow of current.
A thin layer applied to the surface of solar cells to minimize light reflection, increasing absorption and efficiency.
